newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Kiev says ship's arrest strains Russia relations.
newsitem.headline: Kiev says ship's arrest strains Russia relations.

text.p: Ukraine's foreign minister on Friday accused Russia of straining relations between the neighbouring former Soviet republics after Moscow's forces arrested a Ukrainian ship and its 11-man crew.

"This happened at a very inconvenient moment. We should clarify such situations with diplomatic notes but I do not want to start a war of diplomatic notes. That's the last thing we need now," Hennady Udovenko told a news briefing.
Russian border guards who help patrol Georgia's land and sea borders under a 1994 treaty arrested the "Almaz" on suspicion of smuggling near the Georgian port of Batumi on December 4.
Udovenko said the crew had been released on Friday but the captain was still being detained -- despite a protest by his ministry to the Russian ambassador.
Russia's RIA news agency confirmed that the captain was still being held and said Russian security police were conducting an investigation into the alleged smuggling.

The incident represented a blow to relations between Ukraine and Russia which are complicated by a five-year-old struggle over the former Soviet Black Sea fleet -- on Ukrainian territory in Sevastopol but under Moscow's command.
Georgian border guards accused Russia's forces of completely ignoring the Transcaucasus republic's sovereignty and violating international norms, Interfax-Ukraine news agency said.
Kiev sees Tbilisi as a "strategic partner" as the two countries have pro-Russian separatists to deal with -- in Ukraine's Crimean peninsula and Georgia's region of Abkhazia.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin cancelled six visits to Kiev to sign a friendship treaty before he had heart surgery last month because of the row over the fleet.
Hopes the row could be solved suffered another blow this month when Russia's upper house of parliament passed a resolution that Moscow should reclaim the port of Sevastopol.
